mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of valid passport or national identity document of each director, shareholder, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Department of Home Affairs / issuing national authority of the individual's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill, bank statement, or municipal account, not older than three months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Municipal authority / utility provider / licensed bank

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference and confirmation letter confirming the applicant's banking relationship and good standing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank in the applicant's country of residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, and UBOs against the South African targeted financial sanctions list under the POCDATARA Act, the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, FIC's list of domestic politically exposed persons, and adverse media databases. Although OFAC is not a domestic South African statutory mandate, South African banks and international payment rails used by this business require OFAC and EU sanctions screening as a condition for onboarding and transaction processing; therefore OFAC screening is adopted as a compliance-hygiene standard in the KYC/AML operating protocol.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC eRegister (Companies and Intellectual Property Commission corporate name reservation portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names may be registered in any of South Africa's 12 official languages but must be presented in Latin script and must not be offensive, misleading, or in contravention of Regulation 23 of the Companies Regulations, 2011. A name using non-Latin characters must be submitted with an English phonetic transliteration to facilitate the CIPC automated similarity search.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may make written representations to CIPC within 10 business days under section 12(4) of the Companies Act, or apply to the Companies Tribunal for reconsideration under section 160 using Form CTR142 within 30 business days of the CIPC rejection notice. If the rejection arises from similarity to an existing registered name, the applicant may obtain a letter of consent from the existing registered holder and refile the name reservation through the eRegister portal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for this low-risk business on the condition that the virtual office provider maintains a physical street address in South Africa from which service of legal process can be effected during ordinary business hours. A P.O. Box or postnet address is not acceptable as a registered office. Virtual office arrangements will not negate the requirement to maintain adequate accounting records and a registered office capable of receiving notices.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; approximated at a 5% probability of unannounced inspection for a low-risk standard business with no statutory license. The probability rises materially above 10% if anomalous cash transactions, unexplained third-party funding, or violations of FICA reporting duties are observed by the FIC or the South African Police Service.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008 (Republic of South Africa), as amended by the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024; key sections include s13 (incorporation), s14 (registration), s15-16 (Memorandum of Incorporation), s19 (legal personality), s66 (board of directors), and Schedule 2 (transitional and other provisions).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), a juristic person established under s185 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008, operating under the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1A) accompanied by the executed Memorandum of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1B) and consent forms (CoR 4.1A).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital or escrow requirement is prescribed under the Companies Act 71 of 2008. Shares may be issued for consideration in cash, in kind, or on such terms as set out in the MOI; authorized share capital is fixed by the MOI and may be zero-issued initially.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company be incorporated under the name [Company] (Pty) Ltd in accordance with the Companies Act 71 of 2008, and that the Memorandum of Incorporation filed with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission be adopted as the Company's constitution. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the subscribers subscribe for the shares allotted in the MOI and that share certificates issue upon receipt of payment. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office be established at [address] and notice thereof lodged with the CIPC. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] be appointed as sole Director, [Name] as Managing Director, and [Name] as Company Secretary. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the officers be authorized to open bank accounts, execute statutory filings, and transact all incidental matters.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) — online E-Services transactional portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary name availability search on the CIPC E-Services system, then submit a name reservation application using Form CoR 9.1 with up to two preferred names. Pay the prescribed name reservation fee electronically and await the reservation certificate before proceeding with incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Certified identity documents of all directors/incorporators
Proof of residential address of each director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or objected to, file alternative name choices via a fresh CoR 9.1 within 20 business days, or invoke the CIPC name dispute and restoration procedures under Regulation 14 of the Companies Act regulations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Memorandum of Incorporation and First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Incorporation in compliance with Schedule 2, s15 and s16 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008, incorporating the authorised share capital, director appointment provisions, and any pre-emptive or restrictive clauses. Execute the First Board Resolution and arrange for notarisation of director consents and foreign incorporator signatures, if applicable.
required_dossiers: Notarised powers of attorney for foreign signatories (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Revise any non-compliant MOI provisions against the mandatory provisions of the Companies Act and re-execute the corrected MOI; re-notarise any defective signatures before lodgement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notice of Incorporation Lodgement and Certificate Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) E-Services filing window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1A), executed MOI, name reservation certificate, and director consent forms electronically via the CIPC E-Services portal. Pay the statutory incorporation fee of approximately ZAR 175 (USD 10). Upon verification, CIPC will issue the Certificate of Incorporation together with the allocated enterprise number.
required_dossiers: Certified ID documents of all directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or rejected, cure the identified deficiencies within 10 business days by resubmitting corrected forms via the CIPC portal; any adverse decision may be appealed to the CIPC Review Panel within 30 days of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SARS Income Tax, VAT and Employer Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) — eFiling portal and SARS branch offices
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the Certificate of Incorporation, register the Company for Company Income Tax via the CIPC-SARS integrated registration channel or directly on SARS eFiling. Register for Value-Added Tax if annual taxable turnover exceeds or is reasonably expected to exceed ZAR 1 million, and register as an employer for PAYE, UIF and SDL using the EMP101 application.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and enterprise number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to SARS verification queries on eFiling or at the local SARS branch within 21 days; escalate unresolved VAT or income tax registration disputes to the SARS Legal & Policy division or the Tax Ombud.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Unemployment Insurance Fund and Compensation Fund Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Employment and Labour (DoEL) — Labour Centre and online Labour Activation Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Company with the Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF) as an employer and with the Compensation Fund under the Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993 (COIDA). Submit the employer registration statement, workplace description, and payroll details to obtain letters of good standing for UIF and COIDA compliance.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of directors and prospective employees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Lodge any outstanding registration or correction requests at the nearest DoEL Labour Centre; escalate delayed endorsements to the Provincial head of the Compensation Fund for administrative review.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: National Regulator for Compulsory Specifications (NRCS) under the dtic, and the local Metropolitan Municipality for business premises approval
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: NRCS Letter of Authority for Compulsory Specification VC 9071 (Toys and Children's Articles) and SANS 8124 compliance certification for manufacturing, importing, or selling of toys; supplemented by a municipal business licence for the industrial premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Basic Assessment or Registration under Listing Notices 1 and 3 (GN R983 and GN R985 of 2014, as amended) of the Environmental Impact Assessment Regulations under NEMA; small-scale laser cutting and assembly operations below the listed thresholds require only an environmental registration or declaration of exemption from environmental authorisation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act 39 of 2004 ambient standards — PM10 not exceeding 75 µg/m³ annual and 300 µg/m³ 24-hour averages, plus National Dust Control Regulations (GN R827) for fugitive particulate emissions; National Water Act 36 of 1998 — zero unauthorised discharge to water resources, with any trade effluent discharge to municipal sewer subject to local by-law consent; National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008 — segregated handling of sawdust, wood offcuts, and laser residue with disposal only at a licensed waste facility.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the municipal fire department confirming compliance with SANS 10400 Part T and NFPA 160 for laser operations; structural load inspection certification for equipment mounting per SANS 10160; electrical installation compliance certificate under SANS 10142 Part 1 for all CO2 laser machinery; and an Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 clearance certificate from the Department of Employment and Labour, including ventilation and local exhaust extraction verification for airborne wood particulates and fume control in the laser cutting area.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) – eFiling portal (https://www.sars.gov.za and https://efiling.sars.gov.za)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities establish a South African income tax and VAT presence by registering with SARS; for a (Pty) Ltd, incorporation with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) generates an automatic provisional income tax reference number, but VAT registration requires a separate SARS Form VAT101, supported by Companies Act documents, proof of physical or fiscal address in South Africa, and identity/authorisation documents of directors; foreign-owned entities must appoint a local SARS representative / public officer and apply for an income tax reference number via SARS registration before transacting; threshold-based VAT registration is compulsory for taxable supplies exceeding ZAR 1,000,000 in 12 months.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box system exists. South Africa applies statutory corporate residence and controlled foreign company rules (Sections 9D and 25D of the Income Tax Act). Hybrid mismatch rules under the Taxation Laws Amendment Act 2020 apply OECD hybrid mismatch recommendations and may require elective ordering adjustments; election of payment methods or deemed supply options for VAT is available under Section 21(1)(b) VAT Act but no flow-through classification is permitted.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: ZAR 1,000,000 compulsory turnover in 12-month rolling period; ZAR 50,000 voluntary threshold for non-resident suppliers; goods imported into South Africa are subject to VAT regardless of threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: SARS has no real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping mandate. Tax invoices must comply with Section 20 VAT Act and SARS Notice 1446/2009; electronic tax invoices are permitted using approved electronic data interchange (EDI) XML formats with SARS eFiling. Full electronic invoicing (Peppol-style) is under development but not yet mandatory for private companies. SARS may request digital records and API-enabled reporting for eFiling VAT201 submissions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of movable goods qualify for zero-rating under Section 11(1)(a) if the goods are supplied to an exporter and exported within 12 months, or under Section 11(1)(c) where the supplier has proof that goods were delivered to, and removed from, South Africa within the prescribed period; costs/transport charges incidental to export (Section 11(1)(l)) and international services (Section 11(2)(l)) may also be zero-rated. The supplier must retain documentary proof of physical export and the foreign currency consideration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / Truck Manifest
Inward Remittance Certificate (foreign exchange receipt from SARB-approved bank)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or unsupported zero-rating is an offence under Tax Administration Act and VAT Act. SARS will disallow the zero-rating, assess 15% VAT plus 10% to 200% understatement penalty (Section 223 TAA), apply interest, and can pursue criminal prosecution for tax evasion; directors are personally liable for undeclared VAT/TAA civil penalties. Export claims must be supported by evidence for at least 5 years and may be clawed back retroactively if documentation fails.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) and authorised dealers under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933 and the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African Rand (ZAR) is fully convertible for current-account transactions, including trade in goods and services, subject to documentary compliance and authorised-dealer processing. Capital-account flows, such as equity injections, intercompany loans, and loan repayments, require exchange-control reporting or prior approval through FinSurv, particularly for non-resident direct investment. Profit remittances and dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders are freely permitted on after-tax profits provided dividend tax has been declared to the South African Revenue Service (SARS), a tax clearance certificate is presented, and the beneficial ownership and anti-money-laundering screening requirements of the Financial Intelligence Centre Act, 2002 (FICA) are satisfied. Practical hurdles include enhanced source-of-funds verification, sanctions-list screening, beneficial-ownership registration at the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), and accurate classification of the cross-border payment under the SARB Balance of Payments (BOP) reporting framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be received in South Africa within 180 days from the date of shipment. Upon receipt, the exporter must surrender the foreign currency to an authorised dealer in exchange for ZAR at the prevailing market rate; the mandatory conversion ratio is 100% of the invoiced amount unless a specific exemption or foreign-currency account dispensation has been granted by the SARB FinSurv prior to the transaction. Any deviation from this rule, including delayed repatriation or unauthorised retention of export earnings offshore, constitutes a contravention of the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961, and may expose the company to statutory penalties and loss of authorised-dealer facilities. The entity must also submit the relevant export incentive declarations and retain supporting documents such as invoices, customs records, and bank settlement statements for audit purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account

Operational Account and FX Hedging Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-Low for purely offshore digital Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs). Offshore EMIs licensed only in the United Kingdom or other EEA jurisdictions cannot provide ZAR-denominated deposit accounts or act as SARB authorised dealers. They may operate in South Africa under the National Payment System Act, 1998 as payment service providers, but only for initiation and collection of payments, not as a treasury clearing hub. The company may use such EMIs as a low-cost gateway for e-commerce receipts from Amazon Pay and Stripe, but funds must be swept daily to a local tier-1 commercial bank account to mitigate settlement risk and comply with exchange-control reporting obligations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: FICA does not mandate a physical branch interview provided the bank applies an enhanced remote KYC process meeting the verification requirements of FICA section 21(2) and the Guidance Notes issued by the Financial Intelligence Centre. In practice, the four tier-1 banks require at least one natural-person director, preferably the chief financial officer or managing director, to participate in a live video call for identity verification and to provide certified corporate documentation, board resolutions, and proof of physical registered office. Remote onboarding is permitted for a low-money-laundering-risk entity such as a CO2 laser wooden puzzle manufacturer, subject to a successful electronic verification of identity documents, beneficial ownership, and source of funds. A physical visit may be requested if any red flag appears during sanctions screening or if the ultimate beneficial owner is a tax resident of a high-risk jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) flagged as a Politically Exposed Person (PEP) or subject to enhanced due diligence due to residency in a FATF-listed jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A signed source-of-wealth declaration supported by audited financial statements for the past three years, bank reference letters from the originating bank, notarised asset sale deeds, independent legal opinion from a reputable South African legal firm confirming non-association with corruption, and SARS tax clearance certificates for all UBOs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: CIPC beneficial-ownership register incomplete or mismatch between directors, shareholders, and filed records
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A consolidated beneficial ownership register (Form CoR 60), certified Memorandum of Incorporation, board resolution adopting the register, and personal passports of all disclosed UBOs showing no criminal or adverse media history.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of clear source of funds for inbound capital injection from a non-resident shareholder or investor
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six-month source-account bank statements from the remitting institution, formal subscription agreement or shareholder loan agreement, certificate of foreign investment, and a sworn affidavit by the shareholder explaining the lawful origin of the funds with documentary trace.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual transaction pattern such as multiple small inbound payments without matching commercial documentation or inadequate export contract evidence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete export agreements, purchase orders, customs declarations, original commercial invoices, transport documents (B/L or AWB), and a treasury policy note explaining the payment and settlement cycle for the Amazon Pay and Stripe rails.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions screening hit or partial name-match against any international sanctions list
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A false-positive affirmation letter from a sanctions compliance consultant or law firm, clear results from OFAC, EU, UK and UN sanctions screening tools, passport and ID copies, and a legal certification that the company and its beneficial owners are not designated persons.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital from non-resident shareholders must be routed through an authorised dealer using the SWIFT MT103 message format with an unambiguous purpose code: BOP code 3000 for direct equity investment and BOP code 3700 for intercompany trade loans. The remittance instruction should name the South African bank and the dedicated Capital Escrow Account; the authorised dealer will log the transaction in the SARB Financial Surveillance Department file and issue an electronic import/export compliance reference. Prior approval under form MP921 is required if the investment is treated as a loan advance or private equity related to share capital. On receipt, the entity must reconcile the cash against the executed subscription agreement or loan agreement, retain the SWIFT confirmation and foreign-exchange settlement certificate, and submit a quarterly BOP report where applicable. The bank will also require the entity’s FICA declaration, proof of CIPC incorporation, valid board resolution, and tax clearance status before activation of the capital account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for imported raw materials and exported wooden puzzles should be executed via SWIFT MT103 messages using standard trade purpose codes (BOP code 2000 for imports of goods and BOP code 1000 for exports of goods). For amounts exceeding USD 50,000 and for transactions involving letters of credit, the entity should use an irrevocable commercial letter of credit (LC) confirmed by a top-tier international correspondent bank; the LC must be issued by the local authorised dealer and advised through the beneficiary’s bank. Direct payments for recurring trading partners may also be cleared through the South African Multiple Option Settlement (SAMOS) system at the national level, but physical cross-border clearance requires correspondent banking relationships. All outbound payments must be prefunded in ZAR or from the foreign-currency account, accompanied by a distribution-voucher, invoice, customs clearance, proof of delivery, and relevant regulatory declarations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward exchange contracts (FECs) on ZAR/USD/EUR/GBP with tenors of up to 24 months directly tied to trade receivables or payables and supported by underlying commercial documentation
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) executed with an authorised dealer to hedge non-ZAR loan exposure or term-export cashflows
European plain-vanilla currency options on ZAR for protection against adverse exchange rate movements on forecasted dividend remittances or import costs

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are generally not permissible domestically for ZAR resident entities because ZAR is fully convertible; NDFs may only be executed offshore by non-resident counterparties writing ZAR exposure, and such transactions do not form part of the domestic treasury plan.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (CIPC e-filing) — statutory confirmation of company status, directors, members, registered office, financial year-end and Public Interest Score
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), South Africa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary of the incorporation date, every year without exception
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Escalating late-filing penalty from approximately ZAR 180 per month (small company band) in accordance with the CIPC non-compliance fee schedule; reclassification from 'white' to 'grey' non-compliant status, blocking certificates of good standing, share transfers and director change filings; continued default triggers a final compliance notice and administrative strike-off/deregistration, usually within 6–12 months of the missed deadline; directors risk personal liability under s26(6) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 if the company trades while non-compliant.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership (UBO) annual declaration and register confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) — Beneficial Ownership Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, bundled with the Annual Return within 30 business days after the incorporation anniversary; each share transfer or UBO change must be filed with CIPC within 10 business days of the register update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Nominal CIPC BO filing fee of ZAR 10 per submission; late or incomplete filings draw administrative penalties, refusal to process share transfers, director appointments and Annual Returns, and fines of up to ZAR 250,000 (or 12 months imprisonment) per responsible director under the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024; persistent non-compliance blocks good-standing certification and supports eventual CIPC strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) — preparation, board approval and, where triggered, independent review report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of Directors of the (Pty) Ltd; AFS retained at the registered office and filed with CIPC only where the Memorandum of Incorporation or the Commission requires it (private company with Public Interest Score below 350 is normally exempt from filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial year must not exceed 15 months; AFS must be prepared and approved by the board within 6 months after each financial year-end; Public Interest Score calculated and certified in the same cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare AFS within 6 months is a directorial offence under s33(5) of the Companies Act, carrying a fine up to ZAR 250,000 and/or imprisonment up to 12 months; s162 delinquency orders may disqualify directors; absent AFS also block lawful dividend declarations, solvency-and-liquidity assessments, SARS return completion and external financing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Compulsory independent audit for any (Pty) Ltd whose Public Interest Score (PIS) equals or exceeds 500 points, or whose PIS is 350–499 unless the company is 'internally managed' (all shares held by directors and no material third-party interests); independent review by a registered accountant is required for PIS of 100–349, and for PIS below 100 where the company is not internally managed; an owner-managed company with PIS below 100 is fully exempt from audit and review. PIS calculation: 1 point per employee, 1 point per ZAR 1 million of third-party liabilities, 1 point per individual shareholder or beneficial holder, and 1 point per director or officer.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for SMEs (adopted under s29(4) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008) for private companies with PIS below 350; full IFRS applies to public companies, state-owned companies, or where the Memorandum of Incorporation voluntarily imposes full IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At each Annual Return the board must re-certify the Register of Beneficial Ownership, submit a UBO declaration to CIPC, and ensure every listed UBO validates their identity through the CIPC BO-confirmation portal. Each share transfer requires: (i) updating the Register of Members and UBO Register on the transaction date, (ii) filing the UBO change with CIPC within 10 business days, and (iii) reconciling all on-site statutory registers against CIPC records during the annual register audit. Discrepancies must be remedied before the Annual Return is submitted.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Statutory Minute Book (shareholder and board resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $160–$640 per annum (ZAR 3,000–12,000) for professional company-secretarial and registered-office services, exclusive of VAT
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Nil where fully exempt (PIS below 100 and owner-managed); independent review ZAR 15,000–40,000 (≈USD 800–2,200); full statutory audit ZAR 40,000–120,000 (≈USD 2,200–6,500) if PIS thresholds are crossed

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (applicable to years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023; reduced from 28%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying Small Business Corporations (gross income ≤ ZAR 20,000,000; all shareholders natural persons; not a personal service or investment holding entity) benefit from progressive rates: 0% on the first ZAR 95,000; 7% on ZAR 95,001–385,000; 21% on ZAR 385,001–550,000; 27% above ZAR 550,000. Additional incentives include the section 11D research-and-development deduction (150% of qualifying expenditure), learnership allowances, and the Employment Tax Incentive. No preferential patent-box or IP regime applies.
